## Working Read

This essay is a structural consent essay, not a simple ethics note. Its job is to explain why consent behaves like a gradient mask: it preserves signal, protects the shared substrate, and prevents optimization from flattening the living system it depends on.

## Core Claim

Consent is not a decorative constraint on optimization; it is the mechanism that keeps optimization reversible, intelligible, and non-destructive.

## Key Ideas

- Consent preserves substrate quality.
- Reversibility is part of consent, not an optional add-on.
- Signal integrity deteriorates when optimization bypasses authorization.
- Future intelligence depends on keeping the system consentful enough to repair itself.

## Open Questions

- What counts as a consent boundary when optimization is distributed?
- How can a system detect consent drift before it becomes structural damage?
- Which signals should remain outside the optimization loop entirely?
